use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: Dual designations are resolved by correlating two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Dual designations are resolved by correlating two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: C2 JU correlates two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation, resolving the dual designation.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Two ballistic missile tracks are reported to the interface and are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
in_scope_actions: Correlate two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface
Process two tracks that pass the second correlation test and have no correlation restriction for dual designation resolution
Resolve the dual designation by correlating the eligible tracks
excluded_adjacent_actions: Using PPLI data to reduce surveillance track reporting redundancy
Minimizing the occurrence/duration of dual designations through broader common tracking protocols
Post-correlation reporting or downstream administrative processing
variant_dimensions: Correlation eligibility conditions: tracks that pass the second correlation test vs. tracks with no correlation restriction

claims.content: C2 JU
Two tracks have been reported to the interface and are recognized by the C2 JU as eligible for correlation.

The two tracks have passed the required correlation tests and restrictions before correlation is executed, including no correlation restriction such as ID conflict, Strength > 1, or conflicting current Mode II code.
Positions of the two tracks tested for correlation have been extrapolated to the same time.

missing_aspects: The claim specifies 'ballistic missile' tracks, but the cited evidence (EC-PC-014) refers generally to 'two tracks'. The specific track type is not supported by the provided evidence.

claims.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The C2 JU compares locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
The two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once and are deemed a tentative correlation.
The same two tracks are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.
The two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and have no correlation restriction, so the C2 JU processes them for dual designation resolution.

The recognizing C2 JU initiates transmission of the J7.2 Correlation message, requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks and identifying the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
In the absence of any prespecified rejection condition, the receiving IUs accept the requested correlation.
If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.

Diverges from Step 4: instead of requiring the two tracks to pass the second correlation test with no correlation restriction, the C2 JU may manually initiate correlation of any two tracks reported to the interface, irrespective of the correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or the requirements in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1h, provided the tracks are not of a different E/C, one simulated and one live, or both remote.

Diverges from Step 4: despite an ID conflict restriction, automatic correlation may be allowed if either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend.

Diverges from Step 6: instead of accepting the requested correlation, a responding C2 JU may transmit a reverse correlation by sending the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 6: when RV is set to 3 and the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held and has an OCC, the C2 JU executes the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.
Diverges from Step 7: when the C2 JU has initiated a J7.2 and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, the Dropped TN is retained as a remote track instead of being dropped.
At main flow step 1, if it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation should occur.

If the JU with R2 has not received any local sensor data since the last transmitted update, or the JU determines that the ballistic missile track is lost by other system criteria, the track is considered lost. Subsequent reports include held data and set the Lost Track Indicator to value 1. A JU reporting a lost track is assumed to have a TQ of 5 less than the reported TQ, and a JU holding Tracking data may assume R2 with that calculated TQ.
The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.

If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator is alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation; or (b) transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.

The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow rejection. If a JU receives a J7.2 Correlation message and holds OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled), it shall reject the correlation. Whenever a correlation request is rejected, a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
If the received J7.2 message contains one or both of the same TNs as contained in the transmission of the own unit's J7.2 message sequence in progress, prescribed actions shall be taken.

missing_aspects: Recovery/continuation after decorrelation (EC-EF-033) is not specified.
Recovery/continuation after the 6-second correlation-test timing violation (EC-EF-012) is not specified.
The specific conflict-resolution actions for overlapping J7.2 messages (EC-EF-041) are not described in the provided evidence excerpt.
Track-loss recovery/resumption path after Lost Track Indicator is set to value 1 is not specified; the evidence states only the interruption and TQ adjustment.
Evidence does not specify the correlation attempt context (step 1), nor does it define the exit condition that 'the correlation attempt is not continued'.
Evidence does not link this condition to 'main flow step 1', nor does it state that 'normal correlation processing is interrupted' as an exit behavior.
Evidence does not mention 'main flow step 2', nor does it describe the consequence/exit ('no recovery is specified') when the timing constraint is violated.
Evidence does not link this to 'main flow step 4', nor does it state that the process 'returns to main flow step 4' or that the conflict is definitively 'resolved' upon taking these actions.
Evidence does not link this to 'main flow step 4' or the 'manual-correlation alternative', nor does it explicitly state 'Exit: manual correlation is not performed'.
Evidence does not link this to 'main flow step 6', nor does it explicitly state 'Exit: the requested correlation is not accepted'.
Evidence does not link this to 'main flow step 6', specify what the 'prescribed conflict-resolution actions' are, or state the exit condition regarding the 'overlapping correlation request'.

claims.content: The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.

Upon acceptance of the correlation, the receiving C2 IUs retain the designated Retained TN and drop the designated Dropped TN; if the originating C2 JU held R2 for the Dropped TN, it also drops the Dropped TN.

Upon correlation execution, the Retained TN is updated with data from the Dropped TN: the specified kinematic data fields (Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track) are transferred.

The Retained TN's IFF/SIF and identification data reflect the transferred Dropped TN data: any nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data from the Dropped TN is present when the corresponding Retained TN data was zero, and identification data is applied in accordance with the ID conflict restrictions.
If the correlation was a manual correlation accepted with RV field set to value 3, the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for 5 minutes.
